If it takes six, eight, ten years, money changes, priorities change, Congresses change, administrations change. So if we can get the money up front and move fast, we think we can get it done very quickly. But if we don't do something now, we won't have five, ten years. This system. This system truly will have failures and people's lives will be in danger.

background.text: but the Secretary's job certainly has some challenges. There are also people out there who assume that you can't have transportation as we've had it in this country and want to see it in the future and protect the environment and do it in a clean way.

ground_truth: Democrats who have a vision, or some liberals or environmentalists, their vision of the environment is you can't build anything. Well, we have to build things in this country. We have to make investments. And so I look at the projects that we want to do. The materials that we use are cleaner. The systems we use are cleaner. The problem is that, again, if we're going to repave a road over the same road, we need to get permits. And it takes years upon years to get permits to build in the same place we already had a road. But, again, it can't take a decade. It can't take 15 years. The former president says, listen, give me an answer. He's a bull in a china shop in many ways where if he agrees with the idea, he'll do all he can. To clear the way to make sure these things get done. It must have been a really hard four years for him where the current president was in office. But the four years, I think, gave him time and space to think through and envision how he wanted the next four years to be. And I think if he had won a second term consecutively, it wouldn't have been the same.
